program_overview.title: KS2 SATs Maths: Arithmetic, Reasoning and Times Tables
program_overview.tagline: Instant times tables, a calm arithmetic paper and reasoning answers that show their thinking, built up over eight months rather than crammed in April.
program_overview.description:
The key stage 2 maths test is three papers. The test framework sets them out plainly: Paper 1 is arithmetic, 40 marks in 30 minutes, and Papers 2 and 3 are mathematical reasoning, 35 marks and 40 minutes each, so 110 marks across 110 minutes in total. In 2027 the maths papers are timetabled for Wednesday 12 May (Papers 1 and 2) and Thursday 13 May (Paper 3). Results come back as a scaled score between 80 and 120, and a score of at least 100 meets the expected standard.

Underneath all of it sit the times tables. The national curriculum expects children to have memorised the tables up to 12 by the end of Year 4, and the multiplication tables check tests exactly that: 25 questions, six seconds each, taken in June of Year 4. A child who still counts up in fives to find 7 times 5 loses time on every paper, so this course starts there.

The course runs in four phases: times tables to instant recall, the arithmetic paper method by method, the reasoning papers question type by question type, and finally full papers under real timing. Classes are live and small, so the teacher sees each child's working, not just the answer, and parents get a short written note every month on what has moved and what is next.
what_makes_this_different: Built from the government's own key stage 2 mathematics test framework: the three papers, their marks and timings, and the resource list children actually use
Times tables first, because the multiplication tables check and every SATs paper lean on instant recall
The arithmetic paper taught as a set of written methods, each practised until it is automatic and checked
Reasoning taught by question type: multi-step word problems, explain-your-answer questions, measures, geometry and statistics
Full papers under real timing in the last two months, marked against the published mark schemes
Calm by design: short daily practice and clear progress notes for parents, not late-night cramming

learning_path.phase_1: Times tables to instant recall: every table to 12 by 12, the related division facts, and timed practice in the multiplication check format
learning_path.phase_2: The arithmetic paper: place value, the four written methods, fractions, decimals and percentages as calculations
learning_path.phase_3: The reasoning papers: word problems, measures, geometry, statistics and explaining an answer
learning_path.phase_4: Full papers under timing: past and practice papers, marked and reviewed, with a calm plan for test week

career_outcomes: Times tables to 12 by 12 recalled instantly, with the matching division facts
Secure written methods for every calculation type on the arithmetic paper
A routine for reading, planning and checking reasoning questions
Experience of full papers under real timing before test week
A firm base for Year 7 maths, whatever the result

phase_1_times_tables.title: PHASE 1: Times Tables to Instant Recall (Months 1-2, Weeks 1-8)
phase_1_times_tables.description: Every table up to 12 by 12 and its division facts, learned through patterns first and speed second. Year 4 children practise in the format of the multiplication tables check; older children use it as a warm-up for the papers.

week_1_2.title: Weeks 1-2: Diagnostic and the Easy Tables
topics: A short diagnostic: which facts are instant, which are counted, which are guessed
The 2, 5 and 10 tables and the patterns that make them quick
Doubling to reach the 4 and 8 tables
Commutativity: why learning 3 times 7 also gives 7 times 3
The 11 table and its pattern up to 11 times 9
A personal fact chart: green for instant, amber for slow, red for unknown
projects: Fact chart started: every fact up to 12 by 12 coloured by speed after the diagnostic
week_1_2.practice: Ten minutes of mixed facts on most days, focusing on amber facts

week_3_4.title: Weeks 3-4: The Harder Tables
topics: The 3, 6 and 9 tables and how they connect
The 7 table, the one most children find hardest, with memory hooks
The 12 table built from the 10 and 2 tables
Square numbers up to 12 by 12
Spotting which facts are still slow and why
Using known facts to work out unknown ones
projects: Fact chart updated: amber and red facts listed with a hook for each
week_3_4.practice: Daily mixed practice weighted towards the 6, 7, 8 and 12 tables
week_3_4.assessment: Month 1 check: 25 mixed facts, untimed, then the same 25 timed

week_5_6.title: Weeks 5-6: Division Facts and Missing Numbers
topics: Division facts from each table, read the other way
Missing number questions such as 6 times something equals 42
Fact families: four facts from three numbers
Multiplying by 10 and 100 using place value
Scaling a known fact: from 3 times 4 to 30 times 4
Recognising factors and multiples
projects: Fact family cards made for the ten facts the child finds slowest
week_5_6.practice: Mixed multiplication and division facts with a short timer

week_7_8.title: Weeks 7-8: Six-Second Recall
topics: Practice in the multiplication check format: 25 questions, six seconds each
Typing answers quickly and accurately on a keyboard or tablet
Staying calm when one fact is missed and moving to the next
Re-testing every fact that was amber in month 1
Using tables inside short calculations
Keeping recall instant with five minutes a day
projects: Fact chart completed: the aim is every fact green
week_7_8.practice: Three short timed checks a week in the check format
week_7_8.assessment: Month 2 check: a full 25-question timed check, scored out of 25

phase_2_arithmetic_paper.title: PHASE 2: The Arithmetic Paper (Months 3-4, Weeks 9-16)
phase_2_arithmetic_paper.description: Paper 1 is 40 marks in 30 minutes, all calculation. Each written method is taught, practised and checked until it is automatic, then mixed under time.

month_3_whole_numbers.title: Month 3: Whole Numbers and Written Methods

week_9_10.title: Weeks 9-10: Place Value and Addition and Subtraction
topics: Place value to ten million and reading large numbers
Column addition with several carries
Column subtraction with exchanging across zeros
Adding and subtracting decimals by lining up the point
Estimating before calculating to catch slips
Inverse operations as a check
projects: Method book started: one worked example per method, written by the child
week_9_10.practice: 20 column calculations a week, each checked by estimation

week_11_12.title: Weeks 11-12: Multiplication and Division
topics: Short multiplication by a one-digit number
Long multiplication by a two-digit number
Short division, including remainders
Long division by a two-digit number
Order of operations with brackets
Choosing a mental method when the numbers allow it
projects: Method book entry: long multiplication and long division set out step by step
week_11_12.practice: 15 multiplication and division calculations a week
week_11_12.assessment: Month 3 test: a half-length arithmetic paper, 20 marks in 15 minutes

week_13_14.title: Weeks 13-14: Fraction Calculations
topics: Equivalent fractions and simplifying
Adding and subtracting fractions with different denominators
Mixed numbers and improper fractions
Multiplying fractions, including by a whole number
Dividing a fraction by a whole number
Fractions of amounts
projects: Method book entry: every fraction method with a worked example
week_13_14.practice: 20 fraction calculations a week, answers simplified

week_15_16.title: Weeks 15-16: Decimals, Percentages and the Full Paper
topics: Multiplying and dividing decimals by 10, 100 and 1000
Multiplying a decimal by a whole number
Percentages of amounts
Squares, cubes and simple powers
Working through a full arithmetic paper in 30 minutes
Checking strategy for the last five minutes
projects: Arithmetic tracker: score and time recorded for every practice paper
week_15_16.practice: One full arithmetic paper a week under timing
week_15_16.assessment: Month 4 test: a full arithmetic paper, 40 marks in 30 minutes, marked and reviewed

phase_3_reasoning_papers.title: PHASE 3: The Reasoning Papers (Months 5-6, Weeks 17-24)
phase_3_reasoning_papers.description: Papers 2 and 3 are 35 marks and 40 minutes each, and they test whether a child can use maths in context and explain it. Each question type is taught on its own, then mixed.

week_17_18.title: Weeks 17-18: Multi-Step Word Problems
topics: Reading a word problem twice and finding the question
Bar models for comparison and part-whole problems
Multi-step problems that combine two or three operations
Ratio and scaling problems
Simple algebra: missing numbers and formulae in words
Showing working so method marks are possible
projects: Problem journal started: one solved problem per question type with a bar model
week_17_18.practice: 10 word problems a week, each with a written plan before the calculation

week_19_20.title: Weeks 19-20: Measures, Money and Time
topics: Converting units of length, mass and capacity
Money problems with change and value-for-money comparisons
Reading and calculating with time, including timetables
Perimeter and area of rectangles and compound shapes
Area of triangles and parallelograms
Volume of cuboids
projects: Problem journal entry: a measures question for each unit type
week_19_20.practice: 12 measures questions a week in reasoning-paper style
week_19_20.assessment: Month 5 test: a 20-minute reasoning section, marked against a published scheme

week_21_22.title: Weeks 21-22: Geometry and Statistics
topics: Angles on a line, around a point and in triangles and quadrilaterals
Measuring and drawing angles with a protractor
Properties of 2-D and 3-D shapes, including circles
Coordinates in four quadrants, translations and reflections
Reading line graphs, tables and pie charts
Calculating and interpreting the mean
projects: Problem journal entry: geometry and statistics questions with labelled diagrams
week_21_22.practice: 12 geometry and statistics questions a week

week_23_24.title: Weeks 23-24: Explain, Show and Check
topics: Explain-your-answer questions and what a full answer includes
Always, sometimes or never true statements
Spotting and correcting a mistake in someone else's working
Checking that an answer is sensible in context
Mixed reasoning sets that do not announce their topic
Pacing a 40-minute paper
projects: Explanation bank: model answers to ten explain questions, written in the child's own words
week_23_24.practice: One full reasoning paper a week under timing
week_23_24.assessment: Month 6 test: a full reasoning paper, 35 marks in 40 minutes, marked and reviewed

phase_4_full_papers.title: PHASE 4: Full Papers Under Timing (Months 7-8, Weeks 25-32)
phase_4_full_papers.description: No new content. Full sets of three papers under real timing, marked against the published mark schemes, with a short review after each one and a calm plan for test week.

week_25_26.title: Weeks 25-26: First Full Sets

Marking against the published mark scheme

week_27_28.title: Weeks 27-28: Targeted Repair

Arithmetic speed drills on the slowest methods
Reasoning questions of the types most often dropped
Reading questions aloud in the head before answering
Leaving and returning to a hard question
Checking answers in the final minutes

week_29_30.title: Weeks 29-30: Final Sets

Review of every lost mark
Mixed practice from the repair list
Arithmetic in under 30 minutes with checking time left
Reasoning pacing: 40 minutes per paper
Confidence from seeing the tracker rise

week_31_32.title: Weeks 31-32: Calm Before the Tests

What to expect on each day of test week
Sleep, breakfast and a normal routine
A short talk with parents about keeping test week low-pressure

faqs.question: What is in the KS2 SATs maths test?
faqs.answer: Three papers. Paper 1 is arithmetic, 40 marks in 30 minutes. Papers 2 and 3 are mathematical reasoning, 35 marks and 40 minutes each. That is 110 marks over 110 minutes in total, set out in the government's key stage 2 mathematics test framework.

faqs.question: When are the KS2 SATs maths papers in 2027?
faqs.answer: The government's primary assessment dates page timetables maths Papers 1 and 2 for Wednesday 12 May 2027 and Paper 3 for Thursday 13 May 2027. The multiplication tables check for Year 4 runs in a two-week window from Monday 7 June 2027.

faqs.question: What score does my child need in SATs maths?
faqs.answer: Results are scaled scores from 80 to 120. A scaled score of at least 100 means the child has met the expected standard. The number of raw marks needed for 100 can change from year to year, because the difficulty of the tests varies.

faqs.question: What is the Year 4 multiplication tables check?
faqs.answer: A short on-screen check taken in June of Year 4. Each child answers 25 times tables questions up to 12 by 12, with six seconds for each one. It checks instant recall, which is why this course spends its first two months on times tables.

faqs.question: Can children use a calculator in the SATs maths test?
faqs.answer: The resource list in the test framework is a pen or pencil, a ruler and an optional rubber for the arithmetic paper, plus an angle measurer or protractor and a mirror for the reasoning papers. A calculator is not on it, so this course teaches every calculation by hand.

faqs.question: Is SATs maths the same as 11 plus maths?
faqs.answer: No. SATs are national tests taken by Year 6 children in England. The 11 plus is a selection test set by some areas and schools, usually in Year 5 or early Year 6, with its own format. There is overlap in the maths, and we also run a separate 11 plus maths course.

faqs.question: Are the SATs changing?
faqs.answer: The government has said future assessment arrangements are under review after the Curriculum and Assessment Review, and that arrangements for the 2026 to 2027 academic year will stay the same. We follow the published framework and will update the course if anything changes.

faqs.question: How are the classes run?
faqs.answer: Live online classes with a real teacher, either in a group of 15 to 20 children at a similar level or one to one. Practice is short and frequent, and parents get a written note each month. Current fees for your region are shown in the pricing section of this page.

faqs.question: My child is in Year 4. Is it too early?
faqs.answer: Not for times tables and arithmetic. Year 4 is when the multiplication check happens, and secure tables make every later year easier. Younger children follow the first two phases at their own pace and join the paper practice later.

faqs.question: Can we try a lesson first?
faqs.answer: Yes. Book a free demo class. The teacher plays a few times tables games and arithmetic questions with your child, sees where they are, and suggests whether group or one-to-one teaching fits better. There is no obligation to enrol.
